title: Wait on the Lord, Ye Heirs of Hope
description: Wait on the Lord, Ye Heirs of Hope in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 529, “The Patient Waiting upon God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Wait on the Lord, ye heirs of hope, And let His word sup-port your souls; Well can He bear your cou-rage up, And all your foes and fears con-trol.

lines: Wait on the Lord, ye heirs of hope,
And let His word support your souls;
Well can He bear your courage up,
And all your foes and fears control.
He waits His own well-chosen hour
Blest are the humble souls that wait
With sweet submission to His will;
And in the midst of storms are still; —
Still, till their Father's well-known voice
Then earth grows vocal with His praise,
And heaven the grateful shout prolongs.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
